activities.title: Sounds letters make
body: Each letter has a common sound. The letter b says /b/ as in ball.
Say the sound, then blend sounds together to read a word: /k/ /a/ /t/ reads cat.

questions.prompt: Which word starts with the /s/ sound?
questions.hint: Say each word slowly and listen to the first sound.

questions.prompt: Which word starts with the /k/ sound?

activities.title: Words you learn by sight
body: Sight words are common words you learn to recognize quickly, such as the, said, want, and were.
Many of them do not follow the usual sound rules, so practice seeing the whole word.

questions.prompt: Which spelling is the word said?
questions.hint: The ai makes the e sound here.

questions.prompt: Do you ___ to play? Choose the word.
questions.hint: You use it to say you wish for something.

questions.prompt: Which spelling is the word were?
questions.hint: The w comes first, then e-r-e.

activities.title: What a text is mostly about
body: The main idea is what a passage is mostly about. Details support it.
Example: Bees collect nectar. They make honey in the hive. Honey feeds the colony. The main idea is that bees make honey to feed their colony.

questions.prompt: Bees collect nectar. They make honey in the hive. Honey feeds the colony. What is the main idea?
choices: Bees make honey to feed their colony
questions.hint: Which choice covers all three sentences?

questions.prompt: Rain fell all day. Puddles grew on the road. Kids stayed inside. What is the main idea?
choices: Rain fell all day and changed the day
questions.hint: Which choice describes what the whole passage is about?

questions.prompt: Which best describes a main idea?
choices: A sentence about one small fact
A statement of what the text is mostly about
questions.hint: The main idea is broader than any one detail.
